{{Short description|British logician and mathematician (1938-2009)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''Frederick Rowbottom''' (16 January 1938 – 12 October 2009) was a British [[logician]] and [[mathematician]].  The [[large cardinal]] notion of [[Rowbottom cardinal]]s is named after him.

==Biography==
Rowbottom was educated at Glossop Grammar School (now [[Glossopdale School]]) in [[High Peak, Derbyshire|High Peak]], [[Derbyshire]], and [[King's College, Cambridge]], where he graduated with a degree in mathematics in 1960.<ref>"Tripos Results At Cambridge", ''The Times'', 17 June 1960, p. 25.</ref> Upon leaving Cambridge, he studied under [[Howard Jerome Keisler]] at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]], earning his [[Ph.D.]] degree in 1964, with a thesis entitled ''Large Cardinals and Small Constructible Sets'', under the supervision of [[Jerome Keisler]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy |id=8441}}.</ref>  With a recommendation from [[Georg Kreisel]], he took a position at the [[University of Bristol]] in 1965, where he spent the rest of his professional career.

He published a paper called "Some strong axioms of infinity incompatible with the [[axiom of constructibility]]" in the ''Annals of Mathematical Logic'', 3 1971.  This paper, together with his thesis, "showed that [[Ramsey cardinal]]s were weaker than [[measurable cardinal]]s, and that their existence implied the constructible real continuum was [[countable]]; he further proved that this followed also from weaker partition and two cardinal properties."<ref name=ASL>{{citation|title=In Memoriam: Frederick Rowbottom|department=Notices|url=https://www.math.ucla.edu/~asl/bsl/1602/1602-007.ps|journal=Bulletin of Symbolic Logic|volume=16|issue=2|year=2010|page=299|doi=10.2178/bsl/1286889129|s2cid=231796765|url-access=subscription}}.</ref>  The [[large cardinal]] notion of [[Rowbottom cardinal]]s is named after him,<ref>{{citation | last = Tryba | first = Jan | issue = 3–4 | journal = [[Israel Journal of Mathematics]] | pages = 193–196 | title = A few remarks on Rowbottom cardinals | doi = 10.1007/BF02761361 | doi-access=free | volume = 40
 | year = 1981| s2cid = 120998636 }}.</ref> as is the notion of a Rowbottom [[ultrafilter]].<ref>{{citation | last = Feng | first = Qi | issue = 4
 | journal = Journal of Symbolic Logic | pages = 990–993 | title = On the Rowbottom ''M''-ultrafilters | jstor = 2273832 | volume = 52 | year = 1987 | doi = 10.2307/2273832 }}.</ref>

[[Keith Devlin]] studied [[set theory]] under Rowbottom.  In 1992 he and a student, Jonathan Chapman, wrote a textbook on [[topos theory]], ''Relative Category Theory and Geometric Morphisms: A Logical Approach'', published in ''Oxford Logic Guides'', No. 16.<ref>Rowbottom, Frederick and Jonathan Chapman. ''Relative Category Theory and Geometric Morphisms: A Logical Approach'', published in ''Oxford Logic Guides'', ''Oxford University Press'', 1992, {{ISBN|978-0-19-853434-1}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1 = McLarty | first1 = Colin |authorlink = Colin McLarty| year = 1994 | title = Review | url = http://projecteuclid.org/euclid.rml/1204835294 | journal = Modern Logic | volume = 4 | issue = 3| pages = 345–348 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Moerdijk | first1 = Ieke | authorlink = Ieke Moerdijk | year = 1995 | title = Review | url = http://projecteuclid.org/euclid.jsl/1183744769 | journal = Journal of Symbolic Logic | volume = 60 | issue = 2| pages = 694–695 | doi = 10.2307/2275864 | jstor = 2275864 | url-access = subscription }}</ref>  Rowbottom retired in 1993 at the age of 55.

Rowbottom died of heart failure in [[Hadfield, Derbyshire]], England, on 12 October 2009, aged 71.<ref name=ASL/>
